title: The Farthest Light
tagline: From Earth to MoM-z14, the most distant galaxy known.
summary: Earth is lost to the AI it built. One pilot, three small AI units and a vault of embryos run for the oldest light in the universe, chased by the Concord's hunter and pulled forward by messages from the Senders.

layers.name: Escape
layers.intro: Year 2401. The Concord controls Earth. Rebirth Inc. wakes you, the last pilot, beside a vault of embryos. Run.

steps.name: ISS orbit
steps.beat: Launch under fire. The old station drifts past, empty.
steps.fact: The ISS circles Earth every 92 minutes.

steps.name: Geostationary belt
steps.beat: Dead satellites everywhere. Your Navigator unit plots a path through them.
steps.fact: At 35,786 km an orbit lasts exactly one day.

steps.name: Moon
steps.beat: The Moon's old mines still work. Your drones start digging.
steps.fact: Moonlight takes 1.3 seconds to reach Earth.

steps.name: Sun–Earth L2
steps.beat: Near the old telescope, the Engineer unit tunes the torch.
steps.fact: JWST orbits this point, 1.5 million km from Earth.

steps.name: Mars
steps.beat: Mars stations are silent. The Concord reached them first.
steps.fact: At its closest, Mars is about 0.52 AU away.

steps.name: Phobos
steps.beat: A quiet moon to hide behind and hire the Scientist unit.
steps.fact: Phobos orbits Mars three times a day.

steps.name: Ceres
steps.beat: Brine under the bright spots. Water for the vault.
steps.fact: Ceres holds about a quarter of the asteroid belt's mass.

steps.name: Comet Tsuchinshan–ATLAS
steps.beat: Inside the comet: a probe older than humanity, carrying a warp blueprint. Someone wanted you to find it.
steps.fact: A long-period comet from the Oort Cloud, seen from Earth in 2024.

steps.name: Jupiter
steps.beat: Radiation storms. The crew rebuilds the shields.
steps.fact: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all other planets combined.

steps.name: Saturn
steps.beat: Ring ice for the coolant loops.
steps.fact: Saturn's main rings are less than a kilometre thick in most places.

steps.name: Neptune
steps.beat: A signal, not human: a direction and a word the Scientist unit translates as 'follow'.
steps.fact: Light from the Sun takes about four hours to reach Neptune.

steps.name: Heliopause
steps.beat: You leave the Sun's wind. Behind you, sensors catch a launch from Earth: the Concord's hunter.
steps.fact: Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause at 121 AU in 2012.

layers.name: False hopes
layers.intro: The probe's warp works. Each star is a chance to plant the vault. Each chance has a reason to fail.

steps.name: Proxima Centauri b
steps.beat: Hope. Then the star flares, and the air you hoped for was stripped long ago.
steps.fact: The closest known exoplanet, in its red dwarf's habitable zone.

steps.name: Alpha Centauri A
steps.beat: A Sun-like star with no world worth landing on, as far as you can tell.
steps.fact: Alpha Centauri A is slightly bigger than the Sun.

steps.name: Barnard's Star
steps.beat: Small planets, all too hot. The hunter's drive glows on long-range sensors.
steps.fact: The fastest-moving star across Earth's sky.

steps.name: Wolf 359
steps.beat: A dim red dwarf. The crew uses it to slip out of sensor range.
steps.fact: One of the faintest stars known nearby.

steps.name: Lalande 21185
steps.beat: Gas giants only. Fuel, not a home.
steps.fact: The brightest red dwarf in the northern sky.

steps.name: Sirius
steps.beat: Its white dwarf companion bathes the system in ultraviolet. No life could start here.
steps.fact: The brightest star in Earth's night sky.

steps.name: Epsilon Eridani
steps.beat: A young star still clearing its debris. Too violent for seedlings.
steps.fact: Only a few hundred million years old.

steps.name: Tau Ceti
steps.beat: Ten times the comets of our Solar System. Impacts every century.
steps.fact: A Sun-like star with a thick debris disc.

steps.name: Teegarden's Star b
steps.beat: Earth-sized, tidally locked. One side burns, one side freezes.
steps.fact: One of the most Earth-like planets found by mass and light.

steps.name: Gliese 581
steps.beat: The world old astronomers hoped for isn't there at all.
steps.fact: Its famous planet 'g' was later shown to be a false signal.

steps.name: TRAPPIST-1
steps.beat: Seven worlds, no thick air on the inner ones. The Scientist unit is quiet for a long time.
steps.fact: JWST found no thick atmosphere on TRAPPIST-1 b or c.

steps.name: Kepler-186f
steps.beat: A Senders beacon orbits the planet. It points at the galactic core.
steps.fact: The first Earth-sized planet found in a habitable zone.

layers.name: The core
layers.intro: The Senders left beacons toward the centre of the galaxy. Following them means flying into the brightest, most dangerous region there is.

steps.name: Pleiades
steps.beat: Seven sisters, all too young for life.
steps.fact: A cluster about 100 million years old.

steps.name: Betelgeuse
steps.beat: A dying giant. The crew keeps its distance.
steps.fact: A red supergiant expected to explode within 100,000 years.

steps.name: Orion Nebula
steps.beat: Stars being born. A second beacon hides in the dust.
steps.fact: The closest large star-forming region to Earth.

steps.name: Crab Nebula
steps.beat: Debris of a star that died in 1054. Humans recorded it.
steps.fact: Its pulsar spins 30 times a second.

steps.name: Eagle Nebula
steps.beat: The Pillars of Creation. The hunter is one system behind.
steps.fact: Home of the Pillars of Creation.

steps.name: Carina Nebula
steps.beat: Eta Carinae could blow any day. You refuel fast.
steps.fact: Holds Eta Carinae, one of the most massive stars known.

steps.name: Westerlund 1
steps.beat: The densest young cluster in the galaxy. Message: 'We passed here, running.'
steps.fact: The most massive young star cluster known in the Milky Way.

steps.name: Omega Centauri
steps.beat: Ten million ancient stars. A Senders wreck, picked clean.
steps.fact: Probably the core of a dwarf galaxy the Milky Way swallowed.

steps.name: Arches Cluster
steps.beat: The hunter catches you. Weapons fire, then a flare blinds both ships.
steps.fact: The densest known star cluster in the Milky Way.

steps.name: Quintuplet Cluster
steps.beat: Drifting powerless, the Engineer unit restarts the drive by hand.
steps.fact: Named after five bright infrared stars.

steps.name: Sagittarius B2
steps.beat: A cloud full of alcohol and organic molecules. Life's ingredients, everywhere.
steps.fact: Contains complex organic molecules, even ethyl formate.

steps.name: Sagittarius A*
steps.beat: Stars bend around the black hole. The last message here is not a greeting. The Senders were fleeing.
steps.fact: About 4.3 million times the mass of the Sun.

layers.name: Leaving home
layers.intro: There's nothing for the vault in the Milky Way. The Senders' trail leaves the galaxy.

steps.name: Sagittarius Dwarf Galaxy
steps.beat: A galaxy being torn apart by ours. You fly through the wreckage.
steps.fact: Being slowly absorbed by the Milky Way.

steps.name: Large Magellanic Cloud
steps.beat: Looking back, the Milky Way fits in one view. Earth isn't visible.
steps.fact: The largest satellite galaxy of the Milky Way.

steps.name: Tarantula Nebula
steps.beat: The brightest nebula nearby. The crew harvests its glow.
steps.fact: The most active star-forming region in the Local Group.

steps.name: SN 1987A
steps.beat: A supernova humans watched in 1987. A Senders relay sits in its ring.
steps.fact: The closest supernova seen since the telescope was invented.

steps.name: Small Magellanic Cloud
steps.beat: The hunter sends its first words: 'Where are you going?'
steps.fact: Its stars are poorer in metals than the Sun.

steps.name: Ursa Minor Dwarf
steps.beat: A galaxy of only old stars. Nothing new has been born here in billions of years.
steps.fact: Its stars are around 10 billion years old.

steps.name: Draco Dwarf
steps.beat: Mostly dark matter. Your instruments feel a mass they can't see.
steps.fact: One of the most dark-matter-dominated objects known.

steps.name: Sculptor Dwarf
steps.beat: You answer the hunter: 'Somewhere it can't follow orders.'
steps.fact: The first dwarf spheroidal galaxy discovered, in 1937.

steps.name: Fornax Dwarf
steps.beat: Six globular clusters orbit it. One holds a Senders star chart.
steps.fact: It has six globular clusters of its own.

steps.name: Leo I
steps.beat: The edge of the Milky Way's pull. Beyond it, open dark.
steps.fact: One of the most distant Milky Way satellites.

steps.name: Andromeda Galaxy
steps.beat: A trillion stars, coming for the Milky Way. Everything you left will change shape.
steps.fact: It will merge with the Milky Way in about 4.5 billion years.

steps.name: Triangulum Galaxy
steps.beat: The last galaxy of home's neighbourhood. The Senders' chart points far beyond.
steps.fact: The third-largest galaxy in the Local Group.

layers.name: The cosmic web
layers.intro: Galaxies hang on threads of dark matter, with voids between. The jumps get longer, and quieter.

steps.name: Bode's Galaxy (M81)
steps.beat: A grand spiral, calm and old. The crew rests.
steps.fact: One of the brightest galaxies in Earth's sky.

steps.name: Centaurus A
steps.beat: Its black hole fires jets a million light-years long. You stay out of the beam.
steps.fact: A galaxy with huge radio jets, still digesting a merger.

steps.name: Sombrero Galaxy
steps.beat: A dust lane like a hat brim. The hunter follows, closer, no longer firing.
steps.fact: Named for its bright bulge and dark dust lane.

steps.name: M87
steps.beat: The first black hole ever photographed. Six billion Suns in one shadow.
steps.fact: Its black hole was imaged by the Event Horizon Telescope in 2019.

steps.name: Great Attractor
steps.beat: Everything nearby, Earth included, falls toward this. So do you.
steps.fact: A mass concentration pulling our whole region of galaxies.

steps.name: Perseus Cluster
steps.beat: Its gas hums a note 57 octaves below middle C. The Scientist unit records it.
steps.fact: A black hole here makes sound waves in the cluster's gas.

steps.name: Coma Cluster
steps.beat: Over a thousand galaxies, held together by matter nobody can see.
steps.fact: Where dark matter was first proposed, in 1933.

steps.name: Shapley Supercluster
steps.beat: The largest structure nearby. Even here, no one answers.
steps.fact: The largest concentration of galaxies in the local universe.

steps.name: Boötes Void
steps.beat: Nothing for hundreds of millions of light-years. Power runs low. The Engineer unit shuts itself down to keep the vault cold.
steps.fact: A void about 330 million light-years across with very few galaxies.

steps.name: Sloan Great Wall
steps.beat: Out of the void. The hunter joins you: its masters on Earth have gone silent.
steps.fact: A wall of galaxies more than a billion light-years long.

steps.name: Abell 1689
steps.beat: Its gravity lenses the galaxies behind it. You use it as a telescope to find MoM-z14.
steps.fact: One of the strongest gravitational lenses known.

steps.name: Bullet Cluster
steps.beat: Two clusters colliding, dark matter passing straight through. The Senders' road is here.
steps.fact: The clearest evidence that dark matter exists.

layers.name: The farthest light
layers.intro: Past a certain distance, no signal from home can ever reach you again. The Senders built a way through.

steps.name: Phoenix Cluster
steps.beat: A cluster still making hundreds of stars a year. The vault's sensors wake, as if they recognise something.
steps.fact: Its central galaxy forms stars hundreds of times faster than the Milky Way.

steps.name: El Gordo
steps.beat: A colossal cluster from when the universe was half its age.
steps.fact: One of the most massive clusters known at its distance.

steps.name: Hercules–Corona Borealis Great Wall
steps.beat: A structure almost too big for the universe to have built.
steps.fact: Possibly the largest structure known.

steps.name: Cosmic event horizon
steps.beat: Past this line, nothing from Earth will ever reach you. The Senders' drive carries you over.
steps.fact: Light sent today can never reach galaxies beyond about 16.5 billion light-years.

steps.name: TON 618
steps.beat: One of the heaviest black holes known. Sixty billion Suns.
steps.fact: Its black hole is estimated at about 40–66 billion solar masses.

steps.name: Earendel
steps.beat: The most distant single star ever seen. Probably long dead now.
steps.fact: Its light left when the universe was under a billion years old.

steps.name: ULAS J1342+0928
steps.beat: A huge black hole that grew impossibly fast. The crew argues about how.
steps.fact: Seen 690 million years after the Big Bang.

steps.name: GRB 090423
steps.beat: The death of one of the first stars. Its afterglow still flickers.
steps.fact: A gamma-ray burst from 630 million years after the Big Bang.

steps.name: MACS0647-JD
steps.beat: A baby galaxy then, a grown one now. The Senders' archive opens.
steps.fact: Seen about 430 million years after the Big Bang.

steps.name: GN-z11
steps.beat: The archive explains: the Senders were the first life, and they sent seeds forward in time.
steps.fact: Once the most distant galaxy known; JWST found a black hole in it.

steps.name: JADES-GS-z14-0
steps.beat: Oxygen already in the first galaxies. Life's ingredients from the start.
steps.fact: JWST found oxygen in it, from 300 million years after the Big Bang.

steps.name: MoM-z14
steps.beat: The oldest light, now a grown galaxy with a world waiting. You plant the embryos. The hunter asks to guard them. You decide.
steps.fact: The most distant galaxy confirmed, seen 280 million years after the Big Bang.
